desc:
A Magento migration and upgrade service moves your products, customers and orders to or from Magento, including the step from Magento 1 to Magento 2. Ecom Swift LLC maps the data, tests the import and checks the numbers before your store goes live.

## What is a Magento migration?

A Magento migration is the move of store data from one platform or version to another. The data includes products and categories, attributes and images, customers, past orders and often reviews and content pages. You may be moving into Magento from Shopify, WooCommerce or BigCommerce, or upgrading an old Magento 1 store into Magento 2.

A migration is more than a copy. Fields in the old system rarely match the new one, so each item must be mapped, tested and checked.

## Why migrations go wrong, and how to prevent it

The common failures are quiet. Variants lose their options, categories land in the wrong place, order history shows the wrong totals, or old URLs return errors so search visitors reach a dead page. These problems appear after launch, when customers find them first.

A planned migration prevents this with a sequence: map the fields, run a test import, compare counts and sample records, fix the differences and only then run the final import. Redirects from old addresses protect the search visibility you have built.

## How a careful migration affects your business

A clean migration protects revenue during a risky moment. Customers can still find products, log in to see their orders and reach pages from bookmarks or search results. Your team keeps its order history, which matters for returns, tax and support.

It also sets up the new store to perform well. Data mapped properly gives you working filters, correct variants and tidy categories on day one. We describe what we protect, and we cannot promise search positions, because a platform change can shift rankings for reasons outside the data itself.

## What a good Magento migration includes

- A field map between the old system and Magento, agreed before any import.
- Products with attributes, variants, prices, images and categories.
- Customers with addresses, and a clear plan for how passwords are handled.
- Past orders with line items, totals, taxes and statuses, in the packages that include them.
- Product reviews and CMS pages where the package covers them.
- A test import on staging, with record counts and sample checks against the source.
- A final import timed to keep the gap between old and new data short.
- Permanent redirects that send every old product and category URL to its new home.
- For Magento 1 stores, a data upgrade path into Magento 2.
- A written migration report listing what moved, what did not and why.

## How we run the move

We start by examining your current store and counting what exists: products, customers, orders and content. Then we agree what moves, what stays behind and what needs cleanup first.

The test import runs on a staging copy of the new store. You review it, and we compare totals and sample records until they match. When you approve, we run the final import, apply the redirects, check the live store and stay close during launch.

The Basic package moves a small catalog with images and categories, a test import and redirects. The Standard package adds customers, attribute and variant mapping and redirects for products and categories. The Premium package adds orders, reviews and content pages, the Magento 1 to 2 data upgrade, launch day support and a period of fixes.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Remove products and customers you no longer need before the move.
- Export a full backup of the old store and keep it.
- Freeze large catalog changes during the final import window.
- Review the test import carefully and write down every issue.
- Plan the launch for a quiet trading period.

**Avoid:**
- Changing your URL structure without a redirect plan.
- Closing the old store before the new one is checked.
- Assuming extensions from the old platform will carry over.
- Approving the import after looking at only a few products.
- Forgetting email, payment and analytics settings on the new store.

## Who it is for

This service suits an owner leaving another platform for Magento who wants products and customers to arrive intact. It also suits a business still running Magento 1 that needs a path to Magento 2. A third case is a store that is changing hosts or rebuilding and needs its catalog moved without losing history.

## What we need from you

Send access to your current store, either by an export file or a staff, collaborator or developer user, plus access to the new Magento admin. Tell us what must move and anything that can stay behind. We never need passwords, and customer password handling is explained during planning, since many platforms do not allow passwords to be exported.
